monstera.name: Monstera
monstera.description: Big, split leaves that unfurl one after another: it grows fast and forgives the odd missed watering.

pothos.name: Pothos
pothos.description: Trailing vines with heart-shaped leaves flecked with yellow: happy on a shelf even far from the window.

sansevieria.name: Snake plant
sansevieria.description: Upright, stiff leaves like swords: water it every two or three weeks and it copes with dim light.

zamioculcas.name: ZZ plant
zamioculcas.description: Glossy, fleshy leaves that store water: ideal for offices and dimly lit rooms.

pilea.name: Pilea
pilea.description: Round, coin-like leaves on slender stems; it often sprouts little plantlets at the base, ready to separate and give away.

felce.name: Boston fern
felce.description: Dense, arching fronds that love humidity: the bathroom is its place, if there's a window.

aloe.name: Aloe
aloe.description: Fleshy leaves full of gel: it wants sun and little water, and does very well on a windowsill.

calathea.name: Calathea
calathea.description: Big round leaves with pale stripes: it wants the soil always just damp, humid air and no direct sun.

alocasia.name: Alocasia
alocasia.description: Arrow-shaped leaves on long striped stems: a showpiece that asks for light and regular watering.

ficus-lyrata.name: Fiddle-leaf fig
ficus-lyrata.description: Big violin-shaped leaves on an upright trunk: it wants plenty of light and doesn't like being moved.

strelitzia.name: Bird of paradise
strelitzia.description: Paddle-wide leaves that fray with age: it wants lots of light and room to grow.

kentia.name: Kentia
kentia.description: An elegant, slow-growing palm with arching fronds: it copes with dim light and the dry air of radiators.

home.title: Houseplants, picked one by one
home.intro: We grow them in our greenhouse and ship them when they're ready, with a card explaining where to put them and how much water to give them.
home.deliveryTitle: From the nursery to your home
home.deliveryText: Fast shipping across Italy for {{cost}}, free on orders of {{freeFrom}} or more.

steps.text: We pick your plant from the ones in the greenhouse, check the leaves and roots, and water it just right for the trip.
We wrap it in paper along with its pot, secure it in the box and hand it to the courier.
It arrives at your door with a card explaining where to put it and how much water to give it.
If it arrives damaged or doesn't settle in, write to us with a photo: we'll send you another.

home.faqIntro: The questions we get asked most often.

faq.q: Do the plants come with a pot?
faq.a: Yes: every plant travels in the plastic pot it grew in. You can leave it as it is or move it to a decorative pot a few centimetres wider.
{{cost}} anywhere in Italy, free when the plants in your basket reach {{freeFrom}}. The threshold is calculated before the discount, so the {{code}} code won't make you lose it.

faq.q: How do I know if a plant is right for me?
faq.a: Every card has three tags: how much light it wants, how much care it needs and how big it is. On the plants page you can filter by your room, the time you have and your budget.

faq.q: Are the plants safe for dogs and cats?
faq.a: Not all of them. {{safe}} are considered non-toxic; {{others}} and the rest can irritate the mouth and stomach if chewed.

faq.q: What if the plant arrives damaged?
faq.a: Reply to the order confirmation email within 30 days with a photo: we'll send you another or refund you, whichever you prefer.

bestsellers.title: Most popular

lightGuide.title: How much light does your room get?
lightGuide.text: Before choosing a plant, look at where you'll put it: light decides whether it will thrive. Pick the option that looks most like your room.
